title: Runtime request contracts, error model, and kernel negotiation notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft outlining the runtime API request/response contract, error taxonomy, and kernel negotiation hints. The goal is a single, pragmatic surface that:
- lets callers express constraints (latency, batching affinity, kernel preferences)
- gives the runtime levers to select kernels/schedulers safely
- produces predictable, machine-actionable error codes for retry/fallback logic

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: hosted + dedicated modes. Private deployments may adopt but can opt-out of some telemetry fields.
- Not in scope: user-facing SDK ergonomics (covered separately), model schema evolution beyond version tags.

High-level request envelope (recommended shape):
- request_id (string): client-generated id for tracing
- model (string): model name, e.g. "redwood-13b-v2"
- model_version (string, optional): exact pinned version or tag
- input (string | array of blocks): input prompt or structured blocks; runtime accepts either string or array for streaming/partial prompts
- max_tokens (int)
- temperature (float)
- top_p (float)
- n (int): number of completions
- stream (bool): whether server should stream frames
- stop (array[string] | string)
- echo (bool)
- batchable (bool, default true): hints whether this request can be batched with others
- priority (enum: low|normal|high): soft scheduling hint
- deadline_ms (int, optional): absolute deadline (ms since epoch) for result
- kernel_preferences (list[string], optional): ordered list of kernel tags nudging runtime (e.g. ["fused-attn", "int8-kernel"])
- kv_cache_handle (string, optional): opaque handle for KV cache affinity; may be absent and runtime will generate one in the response
- kv_cache_hint (enum: prefer_local|allow_remote|no_cache): hint for KV locality requirements
- routing_hint (string, optional): region or tier hint (e.g. "us-west:low-cost")
- client_metadata (map serialized as string): JSON-serialized small object for debugging/tracing

Response envelope (non-streaming):
- request_id (echo)
- request_time_ms
- compute_time_ms
- model (echo)
- model_version (string)
- kernel_used (string)
- kv_cache_handle (string)
- output (string | array)
- token_usage: serialized small object (string)
- warnings (array[string])

Streaming frames:
- FRAME_TYPE: {"chunk","progress","kernel_event","error"}
- chunk frames contain partial tokens and incremental token_usage
- kernel_event frames used to signal a kernel switch or fallback to a different execution path

Error taxonomy and canonical codes (string codes, machine-actionable):
- ERR_VALIDATION: client request malformed, do not retry without change
- ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND: requested model/version unknown, do not retry; suggest model alternatives in message where possible
- ERR_KERNEL_MISMATCH: runtime does not have a kernel satisfying kernel_preferences; fallback candidates provided if available
- ERR_KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE: transient unavailability of a chosen kernel (e.g. initialization), safe to retry with backoff
- ERR_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: capacity limit hit (GPUs/memory); may be retried with backoff or routed to lower-tier model
- ERR_KV_READ_FAILED: KV cache read failed; response will include kv_cache_consistency_hint and whether it is safe to retry
- ERR_KV_STALE: KV cache returned stale version; caller may invalidate local state or accept degraded performance
- ERR_TIMEOUT: deadline exceeded; contains whether partial output exists
- ERR_INTERNAL: non-actionable transient internal error; include trace_id for support
- ERR_COMPATIBILITY: client used deprecated field or incompatible request; include compatibility_advice (see below)

Error payload fields (in addition to code/message):
- retriable (bool)
- recommended_action (enum: fail|retry|fallback|patch_request)
- fallback_models (array[string], optional)
- fallback_kernels (array[string], optional)

Retry semantics guidelines:
- For ERR_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, use exponential backoff with jitter. If fallback_models provided, attempt fallback immediately if latency budget permits.
- For ERR_KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE and ERR_INTERNAL, short backoff (100–500ms) is acceptable up to a small retry budget.
- ERR_VALIDATION and ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND: do not retry; surface error to caller immediately.

Compatibility guarantees and versioning policy:
- Additive fields: safe. New optional fields -> clients that ignore them remain valid.
- Deprecated fields: runtime will accept deprecated fields for at least 12 months and return WARNINGS when present.
- Strict changes (field type change, required new field): will be introduced behind a "compatibility version" header (Runtime-Compat-Version) and a multi-stage rollout.
- Model schema compatibility: model_version is authoritative. If runtime must map model_version to a compatible execution kernel set, it will return ERR_COMPATIBILITY with suggested model_version(s) or kernel_preferences.
- Server-to-client negotiation: runtime will echo a runtime_semver in response (e.g. "runtime:1.4.0"). Breaking runtime changes will bump major version and be announced in release notes; clients may opt-in by setting "Runtime-Compat-Version" header.

Kernel negotiation and selection:
- Goal: runtime chooses the fastest feasible kernel satisfying client hints. Client may provide kernel_preferences; runtime returns kernel_used and kernel_fallback_chain in response or kernel_event frames.
- Selection algorithm (simplified): 1) filter kernels by capability (model arch, quantization), 2) rank by client preferences, 3) apply scheduling-level constraints (availability, warm state), 4) evaluate estimated latency and cost.
- When a preferred kernel is not immediately available, runtime may:
  - return ERR_KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE if the client cannot wait
  - offer fallback kernel and set kernel_event in stream to indicate switch

Scheduler and batching hints:
- Batching affinity key: use kv_cache_handle or an explicit affinity_key to group requests that share KV cache or prompt prefixes to improve caching and prefix-batching effectiveness.
- batchable=false: request is always isolated, cannot be automatically combined.
- Deadline_ms + priority determine scheduler preemption: short deadlines + high priority get early dispatch; long deadline + low priority can be batched.
- Preemptible flag: allow scheduler to pause lower-priority in-flight batches to satisfy high-priority request; experimental, opt-in via preemptible:true.

KV cache semantics and expectations:
- KV cache handle concept: opaque string that ties a request (or series of requests) to a cached key-value (KV) state. Use cases: chat with long context, repeated prefix reuse.
- Cache consistency: eventual. Runtime exposes three modes via kv_cache_hint: prefer_local (best-effort local cache only), allow_remote (can fetch remote), no_cache (bypass).
- Writable vs read-only handles: handles are read-only from client perspective; runtime manages mutation and eviction. If a client needs explicit write semantics (rare), we need a separate API.
- Cache eviction: runtime may evict entries; eviction events surface as kernel_event frames with reason (memory_pressure, ttl_expired).
- Serialization: KV handles point to internal serialized blob; clients must treat handle as opaque. DO NOT attempt to deserialize.

Observability and tracing fields:
- trace_id (optional): propagated through microservices and included in errors/warnings
- telemetry hints: include estimated_token_count to help batching decisions (clients may provide)

Examples (short):
- Example 1: Low-latency chat request that must use local cache:
  {request_id: "r1", model: "rw-7b", input: "hi", batchable:false, kv_cache_hint: "prefer_local", deadline_ms: 1700000000000, kernel_preferences: ["fused-attn"]}
  possible outcome: kernel_unavailable -> kernel_event fallback to "attn-v2" frame -> streamed chunks -> response with kernel_used: "attn-v2"

- Example 2: Bulk embedding-style requests:
  {batchable:true, model:"embed-1", n:1, priority:low}
  scheduler will accumulate up to batching_window_ms or token budget then dispatch

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should kv_cache_handle be composable (allow multiple handles per conversation) or strictly single-handle per conversation?
- Preemption semantics: how to charge compute/time if preempted mid-batch? accounting impact across customers.
- Exactly how long to support deprecated fields (recommend 12 months but ops needs input)
- Backpressure signaling: should we return a specific HTTP header for soft-shed signals?

Next steps and action items:
- Jin: prototype kernel_event frames in streaming path (GH #432)
- Mateo: draft scheduler policy PR capturing preemption accounting (jira:INFR-901)
- Aisha: finalize canonical error code list and map to HTTP status codes (draft v0.2)

References and related artifacts:
- Related: serving-runtime/runtime-inference-api-surface-draft-v1 (internal draft)
- Related: serving-runtime/serving-runtime-api-contracts-kv-scheduling-draft (older notes on scheduling)

Notes to reviewers:
- This document contains multiple operational tradeoffs. Please comment inline on the kernel negotiation and retry semantics sections. If you have telemetry or billing implications, tag the PR/Jira.
